groups.title: TypeScript Core Concepts
groups.question: You are typing the data a Remix loader returns and the update form for a user profile. Explain how you would use TypeScript's inference and type tools.

followUps.Type Inference and Annotation: Where should you write type annotations, and where can you rely on inference?
followUps.Generics and Utility Types: How do generics and utility types help with loader data and form types?

evidence.text: TypeScript infers many types from the values you write.
Function parameters and API boundaries should be annotated explicitly.
Relying only on inference at boundaries can let wrong data shapes spread unnoticed.
Generics reuse logic across data shapes while staying type-safe.
Partial, Pick and Omit build new types from existing ones.
An update form can use Partial of the user type instead of a copy.

groups.title: React Fundamentals
groups.question: Your Remix component re-renders too often, list items lose their state when reordered, and an effect runs in a loop. Explain how React renders and how hooks should be used.

followUps.Component Rendering and the Virtual DOM: How does React decide what to change in the DOM, and why do keys matter?
followUps.Hooks: useState, useEffect, useRef: What do useState, useEffect and useRef each do, and how can useEffect loop?

evidence.text: React compares the new UI tree with the previous one.
It applies only the needed DOM changes.
Stable keys let it match list items correctly between renders.

notEnough: Only saying React uses a virtual DOM.

evidence.text: useState holds values that trigger re-renders.
useRef holds values that persist without causing re-renders.
An effect that sets state it depends on, or has wrong dependencies, can loop forever.

groups.title: Node.js for Remix
groups.question: Your Remix server crashes on an import error and becomes unresponsive when a loader reads a file synchronously. Explain Node's modules and event loop.

followUps.Node.js Module System and ESM: Why does mixing require and import cause errors?
followUps.Async/Await and the Event Loop: Why can synchronous work in a loader slow every request?

evidence.text: Node has CommonJS with require and ES modules with import.
They load differently and are not fully interchangeable.
A project should use one system consistently, with care at the boundaries.
Node runs JavaScript on a single thread.
Synchronous I/O or heavy computation blocks all other requests.
Async I/O lets the server handle other requests while waiting.

groups.title: Development Tooling
groups.question: A null value crashed a Remix page in production, and server-only code accidentally ended up in the browser bundle. Explain your TypeScript and Vite setup.

followUps.Vite and HMR in Remix: How does Vite separate server and client code in Remix?

evidence.text: Strict mode makes TypeScript check for possibly null or undefined values.
Those bugs are caught before the code runs.
tsconfig path settings also help resolve route modules cleanly.
Vite gives fast hot module replacement in development.
It builds separate server and client bundles.
Server-only code must stay in loaders, actions or .server files so it does not leak to the client.
